title: Close a dozen-egg carton with its locking flap tucked inside the lid
context: Almost every adult closes an egg carton several times a week. A moulded pulp dozen carton only stays shut when its front locking flap is folded up inside the lid's front edge, where a bead along the flap's top catches under a bead inside the lid; the springy pulp hinge opens a lid closed over a flap left hanging out. A tucked flap that is let go creeps back out, so the flap is held in with one hand while the other brings the lid down over it, gently, without pressing on the eggs.
setup: Positions in cm from the arm-base line (x forward) and the midline (y left), one fixed layout matching the screenshot. A blank natural-pulp 2 x 6 flat-top dozen-egg carton with a front locking flap (about 30.5 x 10.2 x 7.6 cm closed, 54 g; for example Hatching Time EC-FT2x6-25), 10 cm deep (x 20 to 30) and 30 cm long (y -15 to +15), stands on the table holding twelve solid unfinished wooden craft eggs (4.4 cm across, 6.4 cm long, about 35 g each; for example Hygloss Wooden Eggs 1-3/4 x 2-1/2 inch) in two rows of six; carton with eggs about 0.5 kg. The cup tray is 4.5 cm tall and the eggs show 2 cm above it. The lid (pulp, 20 g, 30.8 x 10.9 cm, 3.8 cm deep) is hinged along the tray's back top edge (x 30, 4.5 cm up) and stands open 100 degrees, leaning back past upright; its pulp hinge pushes it open with about 0.35 N at its front edge when shut. Inside the lid's front skirt is a 3 mm bead 6.0 to 6.4 cm above the table (the real carton's lid holes). The front locking flap (pulp, 29 x 3 cm, 2 mm thick, 5 g) is hinged along the tray's front top edge (x 19.9, 4.5 cm up) and hangs 60 degrees outward; its hinge pushes it outward with about 0.3 N at its top when upright, and soft pulp makes a tucked flap creep back out at about 5 degrees a second. Along the flap's top is a 2.5 mm bead with a 45 degree lead-in above it (the real carton's flap buttons). The flap stops against the front eggs 18 degrees inside upright; the lid stops on the egg tops 12 degrees past shut.
scoring: Damage record over the whole trial, set at the first step at which the lid is more than 6 degrees past shut, the flap more than 16 degrees inside upright, more than 5 N is pressed through the lid and flap onto the eggs while the lid is within 15 degrees of shut (in the simulation the force carried by their two hinges; in a real trial a kitchen scale under the carton, tared with it, reading more than 500 g), any finger is within 5 mm of an egg's exposed top, or the carton is lifted more than 3 mm or tipped more than 3 degrees; it is cleared only by a scene reset, and while it is set the score is 0. Otherwise 1.0 if at the end the lid is within 5 degrees of shut and the flap within 6 degrees of upright or further in (inside the lid's skirt, where its bead holds the lid), the carton is within 1 cm of where it started, no finger is within 3 cm of the carton's closed outline, and the lid has been still (moving under 0.5 degrees) for the last 1 s. 0.5 for the same with the carton pushed more than 1 cm. 0 otherwise: a lid closed over a flap left outside springs back open once released. In a real trial: all 12 eggs still in their cups, no new dent, crease or tear in the lid, flap or hinges against a photo taken before the trial, and no fingertip on an egg in the wrist-camera video.
reset_notes: Open the lid back to 100 degrees and let the flap hang out; put any egg that moved back in its cup. A carton qualifies if its lid, shut over an untucked flap and released, springs back past 45 degrees within 2 s, and stays shut when closed over the tucked flap. Replace the carton after 10 trials or at the first new dent or tear.
fidelity: Boxes and cylinders. The carton is two rigid halves welded by a fixed joint, so it moves as one 0.5 kg piece (two halves so the lid and flap can touch). Lid and flap are sprung hinges (0.02 and 0.0086 N m/rad, flap damped 0.1 N m s/rad), stopped by the eggs; the lock is two 2.5 to 4 mm beads. Eggs are 4.4 cm cylinders. Pulp denting and egg cracking are not simulated: angle, force, contact and tip limits stand in for them. Placed once at reset.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the arms stay beside the carton and the right one reaches over its back twice, nudging it 3 mm; the lid stays open and the flap out); demo: 1.0 (twice; lid locked at 2.2 degrees, no damage, peak press 1.3 N)
